scope: Standalone managed-allocation projection of ProjectCompiler configuration/fingerprint JSON serialization and per-request graph reuse. Two direct UTF8 serializer calls replace UTF16 JSON strings plus UTF8 re-encoding; one thread-safe lazy graph replaces per-snapshot graph serialization.
limits: All elapsed values are permanently unaccepted; the driver records no elapsed fields.
No source reading, source capture, source-file sharing/retry/decoder validation, IO or cache-validation behavior is measured by this projection.
No Roslyn parse/analyze/emit, production publication trust, full-project compilation, time-to-play, peak RSS or Unity/Unreal comparison claim.
The copied candidate ProjectCompiler.cs was NOT compiled during this microproof. Production Graph and ManifestBytes were invoked from a copied existing production DLL.
Manifest PE/PDB inputs are synthetic bytes and are not valid image/symbol proof.
The common driver Request wrapper exists in both arms; the production compiler closure layout is not reproduced. Result byte arrays stay live until validation outside counters in both arms.
48 labeled quality cells include duplicate disabled/no-snapshot count-zero cells; they are not 48 distinct behaviors.
Each fresh process compares complete payload/manifest bytes against its own pre-counter baseline oracle. The frozen app does not export cross-process payload hash vectors.

production_integration.allowed_delta: Exactly two SerializeToUtf8Bytes substitutions; one request-local Lazy<string> with ExecutionAndPublication after existing tool/runtime/generator reads; graph.Value only inside WriteSnapshot. IO, inventory/cache/diagnostic/manifest/publication code otherwise unchanged.

quality.test_config: xUnit.MaxParallelThreads=2; original timeouts and internal concurrent requests unchanged

configuration.source_fixture: Pre-owned ASCII comment strings and source descriptors. Modules are independent in allocation profiles; dependency and order cases are quality fixtures.
configuration.arm_order: Alternates across nine configurations; no reversed pair per configuration, retries or extra cells.
configuration.counter: GC.GetTotalAllocatedBytes(precise:true), whole process around the serialization request. Corpus/oracle creation, explicit GC, complete byte validation and JSON output excluded.
configuration.included_work: Both arms retain the original source Encoding.UTF8+SHA256 work, fingerprint hashing, PE/PDB/source hashing in actual ManifestBytes and complete manifest serialization. Candidate lazy allocation is counted even when no snapshot requests a graph.
configuration.before_each_pass: Clear previous actual result array and force generation 2 GC outside counters. Oracle result arrays remain equally owned in both arms.

allocation_validation.baseline_graph_evaluations: Zero with none; one with one; 2/32/8 with all by shape.
allocation_validation.candidate_graph_evaluations: Zero with none, exactly one with one/all; parallel behavior covered separately in quality.
allocation_validation.sample_variation: All five precise allocation samples are retained, including small/wide variation; no filtering or retries.
allocation_validation.gc_counts: All measured collection counts zero except large/all: both arms have one Gen0 and zero Gen1/Gen2 collections in every measured pass. No general GC-count guarantee is inferred.

quality.shape: 8 fixtures × 3 publication labels × workers 1/2; each cell executes both baseline/candidate. Disabled and no-snapshot are duplicate count-zero operation labels.
fixtures: Unicode/escaping and standard encoder fallback for unpaired surrogates
